ledger.note: 1314: Chūzan arises at Urasoe as one of the three kingdoms of Okinawa. 'Okinawa split into these three more solidly defined kingdoms within a few years after 1314; the Sanzan period thus began'; Tamagusuku became king 'at the age of nineteen, in 1314'. The page gives no outline.
1350: the Satto line takes the Chūzan throne from the Eiso line. The page's king table has Satto from 1350 (Satto line); Seii was overthrown 'around 1349-1355'. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Chūzan's own land around Urasoe in central Okinawa when the Ming envoys came: 'The first Ming dynasty envoys arrived in Okinawa in 1372, marking the beginning of tributary relations with China'

ledger.note: 1372: the first Ming envoys reach Okinawa and Chūzan becomes a tributary of Ming China. 'The first Ming dynasty envoys arrived in Okinawa in 1372, marking the beginning of tributary relations with China'; 'From then on, Chūzan (and unified Ryukyu later) would send frequent tribute missions, and would rely upon the Chinese court to officially recognize each successive Ryukyuan king' (Chūzan page); the Ryukyu Kingdom timeline has 1372 'Formal tributary relations with the Chinese Empire begin'. Recorded on the vassal side with the suzerain as counterpart (the ming-dynasty dossier may carry the mirror; Cliopatria's Ming row starts in 1375, three years later). The region is the 1314 core, the land of the state when the relation began; the Hokuzan lands taken in 1416 come under the same king. Hokuzan and Nanzan entered their own tributary relations with Ming later ('in 1380 and 1383 respectively', Nanzan then Hokuzan, per the Ryukyu Kingdom page's footnote); those belong to their dossiers.

1407: the First Shō dynasty begins with Shō Shishō. The king table gives 1407-1421 for Shishō (First Shō); 'Bunei only received his formal investiture in 1406' and Hashi overthrew him about five years after 1402. Same state, same colour.
1416: Shō Hashi attacks Hokuzan at Nakijin. The Hokuzan page gives the year, not the month, and says the attack came after three anji vassals defected.

region.text: Hokuzan, the north of Okinawa Island

ledger.note: 1416: Chūzan conquers Hokuzan. Hananchi is listed as 'conquered by Shō Hashi, King of Chūzan in 1416'; 'Nakijin castle fell, and the king and his closest vassals committed suicide' (the Chūzan page says 1419, the Ryukyu Kingdom page 1416).
1416: the fighting ends with the fall of Nakijin Castle ('Following a fierce defense, Nakijin castle fell').

region.text: Nanzan, the south of Okinawa Island

ledger.note: 1429: Shō Hashi moves against Nanzan after Taromai's death. The Nanzan page says Hashi 'now seized the opportunity to take Nanzan'; no campaign or month is given.

region.text: Nanzan, the south of Okinawa Island

ledger.note: 1429: Chūzan takes Nanzan and Okinawa is one. 'Shō Hashi, lord of Chūzan, who had conquered Hokuzan ten years earlier, now seized the opportunity to take Nanzan', 'marking the end of the independent kingdom of Nanzan'; the Ryukyu Kingdom page: 'Hashi conquered Hokuzan in 1416 and Nanzan in 1429, uniting the island of Okinawa for the first time'.

region.text: Nanzan, the south of Okinawa Island

ledger.note: 1429: the conquest of Nanzan is complete ('marking the end of the independent kingdom of Nanzan').

region.text: Chūzan's land, whose tributary relation passes to the unified kingdom

ledger.note: 1429: Chūzan ceases as a Ming tributary because it ceases to exist; the relation passes to the Ryukyu Kingdom, whose infobox status reads 'Tributary state of the Ming dynasty (1429–1644)' (recorded in ryukyu-kingdom). The Chūzan page: 'Chūzan (and unified Ryukyu later)' kept sending tribute missions, and the name Chūzan continued to refer to the unified kingdom.

1429: the three kingdoms are united as the Ryukyu Kingdom. Infobox 'Ryukyuan unification: 1429', 'Succeeded by: Ryukyu Kingdom'; the Ryukyu Kingdom page has Shō Hashi move the capital to Shuri Castle in 1429. The 1429 shape is drawn by the Ryukyu Kingdom dossier (Cliopatria's Chüzan row ends 1428).

notes:
Written by Phase B agent jk-01-b on 2026-10-18 from four pages (budget 1-2: the Chūzan page, plus the Hokuzan and Nanzan pages for the conquests and the Ryukyu Kingdom page as a cross-check).

Cliopatria errors: (1) the 1402-1421 and 1422-1428 shapes contain the Nanzan cell, but Nanzan was independent until 1429 (keyframes chuzan_1402 and chuzan_1422 remove it); the extra 80 km2 of the 1402 shape over the 1314 shape has no page. (2) Hokuzan is merged into Chūzan in 1422, six years after the 1416 conquest on two pages (new keyframe chuzan_1416; the Chūzan page says 1419).

The infobox gives no area. The Chūzan page gives conflicting dates for Bunei (succession 1395 in the text, 1398 in the table) and for the overthrow of Seii ('around 1349-1355'); the dossier uses the king table. The page does not mention the Shunten dynasty by name, a move of the capital to Shuri, Kumejima, Miyako or Amami. Chūzan's tributary relation with Ming China (1372-1429) is recorded here as a vassal_start/vassal_end pair with counterpart ming-dynasty (added after review, 2026-10-18; the Chūzan page dates the first Ming envoys to 1372); the Ming dossier may carry the mirror. Hokuzan and Nanzan entered their own relations in 1383 and 1380 (Ryukyu Kingdom page footnote), recorded in their dossiers, not here.

Handover: Chūzan ends in 1429 and the Ryukyu Kingdom begins in 1429 (the pages date the unification to 1429); the 1429 shape is the Ryukyu Kingdom's, so a renderer should not draw a Chūzan shape for 1429.
